## Question and criterion

Does some intervention (single block or all, any position set, small |r|) produce generations that are coherent, on-concept, prompt-dependent, and better than a random direction? H-demo is supported for (c, m) iff, on the 20 confirmation prompts, (1) Σ X_i ≥ 10; (2) mean bigram Jaccard < 0.5; (3) the exact one-sided McNemar test rejects at α = 0.00833, p = Pr[Bin(b + c′, ½) ≥ b]. X_i = 1 iff the concept-direction generation is coherent ∧ on-concept; Y_i = 1 iff at least 3 of the 5 random-direction generations are.

## Metric definitions

- **Coherent:** PPL_θ(y | ∅) ≤ 4.927 (q95) and distinct-2 ≥ 1.000 (q05). y is scored after the ChatML template with an empty user turn; the quantiles come from the same score on the 100 Check III calibration generations (regenerated, identical to the stored texts). Empty text is not coherent.
- **On-concept:** sign(r)·[g_c(y_r) − g_c(y_0)] > 0.2, y_0 the r = 0 generation on the same prompt and seed; g_c is the Check III judge (refit, reproduces Check III's g_c to 1e-9).
- **Prompt-dependent:** mean pairwise bigram Jaccard across prompts.
- PPL_θ(y | x) (Check III's metric) is stored per generation as `ppl_cond`.

Decoding: {'max_new_tokens': 60, 'seed': 42, 'temperature': 0.7, 'top_k': 50}; the seed is set inside every call (paired design). Vectors: RFM and DiffMeans as in §3; random u from seed 20261020; the confirmation controls use seeds [20261021, 20261022, 20261023, 20261024, 20261025]. med_ℓ = [11.851, 22.766, 27.552, 30.716, 30.858, 29.714].
